WHY IT HAS TO EXIST

Digital government stops
at the town hall door.

National portals modernised. Local government, where most citizen contact happens, kept its PDF forms, phone queues and shrinking staff. And the sovereignty question underneath got answered under oath.

F·01

The local gap is measured

The EU’s own eGovernment benchmarking consistently finds local and regional services lagging national ones. Seven in ten EU citizens now use e-government, and hit the thinnest service where they live.

F·02

Some of Europe is far behind

Usage tells the spread: some member states run near-universal digital government, others sit at a quarter to a third of citizens using it. The gap is capacity: small administrations cannot staff a digital department.

F·03

Sovereignty was answered under oath

Asked before the French Senate in 2025 whether it could guarantee French data would never be handed to foreign authorities without EU consent, a Microsoft executive answered that he could not guarantee it. For public administration, that answer is an architecture requirement.

F·04

The staffing cliff is here

Germany’s public-service association counts hundreds of thousands of unfilled public-sector posts. The clerks who remain drown in routine queries that software should have absorbed years ago.

ASKED IF EU DATA COULD BE GUARANTEED SAFE FROM FOREIGN HANDOVER: “NO, I CANNOT GUARANTEE IT”
WHO IT SERVES

For the administrations
closest to the citizen.

The small municipality

The design customer is a local council of a few thousand to a hundred thousand residents: big enough to drown in queries, too small for a digital department. The Desk arrives as a system, deployed on their metal, speaking their citizens’ language, run by the staff they already have.

NO IT DEPARTMENTLOCAL-LANGUAGE DUTYSOVEREIGN BY MANDATESTAFF-RUN

Citizens

Answers about permits, deadlines, documents and procedures in plain local language, around the clock, with the path to a human clerk always one step away.

Clerks & caseworkers

The Desk absorbs the routine query load and delivers incoming requests pre-structured with complete documents, so staff time goes back to the cases that need judgement.

Multilingual communities

Municipalities serving residents in several languages (Malta’s official bilingualism, border regions, migrant communities) get service parity across all of them.

Regional governments

Higher tiers get a deployable pattern: the same sovereign architecture rolled across many municipalities, each keeping its own data on its own infrastructure.

WHAT IT CHANGES

The queue shortens.
The data stays home.

The Desk automates the routine layer of citizen service and structures the rest for human decision, with every byte processed on infrastructure the administration answers for.

Questions answered at once.

The bulk of citizen contact is informational: requirements, deadlines, which form, which office. The Desk answers that layer at once, correctly, sourced from the municipality’s own rules.

Requests arrive complete.

Guided intake checks documents and requirements before submission, removing at the front door the back-and-forth that consumes clerk weeks.

Sovereignty by architecture.

On-premise or EU-sovereign hosting under the municipality’s control: the architecture delivers the guarantee no foreign cloud could give under oath.

THE MECHANICS

A civic system,
shaped like a utility.

The Desk deploys like municipal equipment: installed on local or sovereign infrastructure, loaded with the municipality’s own rules and procedures, operated by administrative staff through plain interfaces.

LAYER 1

The knowledge base

The municipality’s own rules (bylaws, fee schedules, procedures, forms), ingested with versioning, so answers cite the current local text.

LAYER 2

The service engine

Retrieval-grounded answering and guided intake flows, multilingual per the community’s real languages, with confidence thresholds that hand uncertain cases to humans.

LAYER 3

The caseworker surface

Structured queues, drafted responses for approval, and workload views. Clerks supervise the desk; the desk never acts beyond its delegation.

LAYER 4

The sovereign base

On-premise or qualified EU hosting, open standards for records, full audit logs. Compatible in spirit with Europe’s sovereign-workplace efforts, and inspectable by the administration that runs it.
